GHSA-4745-xr3q-p63v.title: `gopass link` creates symlinks outside the store root (Store.Link misses the safePath containment applied to every other fs method)
GHSA-4745-xr3q-p63v.description: ### Summary `internal/backend/storage/fs.Store.Link` builds its destination with a raw `filepath.Join(s.path, to)` and then runs `os.MkdirAll`/`os.Chdir`/`os.Symlink` on the result — without the `safePath` containment check that every other method of the same store backend applies (Get, Set, Move, Delete, Exists, and IsDir/Prune since the fix for GHSA-rw43-4vhf-hcvj, plus the newer `LinkTarget`). A destination name containing `../` components therefore resolves outside the password store root, where gopass creates directories and places a symlink. GHSA-rw43-4vhf-hcvj established that filesystem containment is an intended guarantee of this backend ('safePath already exists and is correctly used by 5 of the 7 Store methods, showing filesystem containment is an intended guarantee, not something being newly requested') in the multi-user, git-synced shared-store threat model; `Link` is the method that fix family missed. Verified on v1.17.3 and still unguarded on current master. ### Details ### Affected product - Package: `github.com/gopasspw/gopass` - Affected versions: **v1.17.3** (tested, tag) and current `master` — the unguarded join is still present (`internal/backend/storage/fs/link.go:49-50`) ### Code path - CLI: `gopass link [from] [to]` — `internal/action/commands.go:729` (registered command, `Action: s.Link`, hidden) → `internal/action/link.go` → `internal/store/root/link.go` → `internal/store/leaf/link.go` → `fs.Store.Link`. - Sink: `internal/backend/storage/fs/link.go:49-50` builds `fromPath`/`toPath` with `filepath.Join(s.path, from|to)` (no `safePath`), then: ```go toDir := filepath.Dir(toPath) if err := os.MkdirAll(toDir, 0o700); err != nil { ... } // :66 arbitrary directory creation if err := os.Chdir(toDir); err != nil { ... } // :70 return os.Symlink(linkDst, filepath.Base(toRel)) // :79 symlink outside the store root ``` `filepath.Join` collapses `..` sequences, so `to = '../../../../tmp/pwned.gpg'` resolves outside the store root. - The leaf-level guard is bypassed: `internal/store/leaf/link.go` checks `s.Exists(ctx, from/to)`, but `fs.Store.Exists` maps a `safePath` error to `false` (`internal/backend/storage/fs/store.go:180-183`), so for a traversal destination the 'destination already exists' check always passes. ### Relationship to GHSA-rw43-4vhf-hcvj That advisory fixed the same class for `IsDir` and `Prune` ('IsDir and Prune are simply inconsistent with the other five') and established that filesystem containment is an intended backend guarantee. Since then: - the newer `LinkTarget` helper (`internal/backend/storage/fs/link_target.go:17`) **does** apply `safePath` — showing new link-related code follows the guarantee; - `Link` — the method that actually *creates* links — was missed and remains unguarded on master. ### Suggested fix Apply `safePath` to `from` and `to` in `fs.Store.Link` before any filesystem operation (deriving `toDir` from the validated path), and reject traversal components at `leaf.Link` as defense in depth; add a regression test asserting that a `to` containing `../` fails without creating anything outside the store root. ### Proof of concept Dynamic proof at the storage layer (Go test executed against v1.17.3): ```go // internal/backend/storage/fs/link_escape_poc_test.go func TestLinkEscapesStoreRoot(t *testing.T) { store := t.TempDir() outside := t.TempDir() // a different directory = outside the store root s := New(store) os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(store, 'x.gpg'), []byte('SECRETDATA'), 0o600) rel, _ := filepath.Rel(store, outside) to := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join(rel, 'pwned.gpg')) // e.g. '../002/pwned.gpg' if err := s.Link(context.Background(), 'x', to); err != nil { t.Fatalf('Link returned error (no escape happened): %v', err) } // -> PASS: symlink created outside the store root } ``` Output: ``` attacker-supplied to = '../002/pwned.gpg' SYMLINK CREATED OUTSIDE STORE ROOT: /var/folders/…/002/pwned.gpg -> ../001/x ``` (The real chain reaches the same sink: `leaf.Link` passes `s.passfile(ctx, to)` to the storage layer, appending `.gpg`.) A full-CLI reproduction: `gopass init && gopass generate x && gopass link x ../../../../../../tmp/pwned` — `ls -l /tmp/pwned.gpg` shows the symlink outside the store. ### Impact The fs backend's containment guarantee (paths must resolve under the store root) is violated on this method: a destination containing `../` components causes gopass to create arbitrary directories outside the store root (`os.MkdirAll`) and place a symlink there (`os.Symlink`). Threat model, following the project's own GHSA-rw43-4vhf-hcvj: gopass stores are multi-user and git-synced, and a remote collaborator with legitimate write access can reach victims through an ordinary sync. Compared with the fixed `IsDir`/`Prune` vectors (where a synced entry name is enough), this one additionally requires a `gopass link` invocation with an attacker-influenced `to`, so we rate it **Medium** like the sibling advisory (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L ≈ 5.4). Consequences: out-of-store directory creation and symlink planting (a foothold for later read/follow operations, since path resolution is lexical and the OS follows symlinks), and breakage of the store-containment invariant that other tooling may rely on.

GHSA-rw43-4vhf-hcvj.title: Path traversal in Prune and IsDir allows arbitrary recursive directory deletion via a crafted secret name
GHSA-rw43-4vhf-hcvj.description: ## Summary `internal/backend/storage/fs.Store` (the on-disk password-store backend) has a `safePath` helper that validates a name resolves to a path under the store root, and returns an error otherwise. `Get`, `Set`, `Move`, `Delete`, and `Exists` all correctly use it. `IsDir` and `Prune` do not: both build their path with a raw, unguarded `filepath.Join(s.path, filepath.Clean(name))`. `Prune` then calls `os.RemoveAll` on that unguarded path. Since gopass is designed around multi-user, git-synced shared secret stores, an entry name containing `../` sequences, arriving via a normal `git pull`/`gopass sync` from another store member, causes `gopass rm -r <that name>` to recursively delete an attacker-chosen directory anywhere the running user has write access, entirely outside the password store. This is distinct from the store-integrity and local-attacker caveats already documented at github.com/gopasspw/gopass/security: `safePath` already exists and is correctly used by 5 of the 7 `Store` methods, showing filesystem containment (operations staying inside the store root) is an intended guarantee, not something being newly requested; `IsDir` and `Prune` are simply inconsistent with the other five. And the attacker here is a remote git collaborator with legitimate write access to a shared store, reaching the victim through an ordinary sync, not the local-machine attacker the threat model explicitly excludes. ## Details `internal/backend/storage/fs/store.go`: ```go func (s *Store) safePath(name string) (string, error) { resolved := filepath.Join(s.path, filepath.Clean(name)) if !strings.HasPrefix(resolved, s.path+string(filepath.Separator)) { return '', fmt.Errorf('path traversal detected: %q escapes store root', name) } return resolved, nil } func (s *Store) IsDir(ctx context.Context, name string) bool { ... path := filepath.Join(s.path, filepath.Clean(name)) isDir := fsutil.IsDir(path) ... } func (s *Store) Prune(ctx context.Context, prefix string) error { path := filepath.Join(s.path, filepath.Clean(prefix)) ... if err := os.RemoveAll(path); err != nil { return err } return s.removeEmptyParentDirectories(path) } ``` `IsDir` and `Prune` both bypass `safePath` and build their own unvalidated path. `internal/store/leaf/move.go`, the call path from a normal delete: ```go func (s *Store) delete(ctx context.Context, name string, recurse bool) error { path := s.passfile(ctx, name) if recurse { if err := s.deleteRecurse(ctx, name, path); err != nil { return err } } ... } func (s *Store) deleteRecurse(ctx context.Context, name, path string) error { if !s.storage.IsDir(ctx, name) && !s.storage.Exists(ctx, path) { return store.ErrNotFound } name = strings.TrimPrefix(name, string(filepath.Separator)) if err := s.storage.Prune(ctx, name); err != nil { ... } ... } ``` `name` reaches `storage.Prune` unmodified (aside from trimming a leading separator), with no traversal validation at any layer above the storage backend. ## POC (available upon request) ## Impact Confirmed directly against `Store.Prune`: given a store rooted at a directory, calling `Prune` with a name containing `../` segments deletes a directory tree completely outside the store root, with no error returned. Since `gopass rm -r <name>` (recursive delete, one of the tool's core commands) passes the given name to `Prune` unmodified, and since the name of an entry in a shared, git-synced store can be set by any team member with write access to that store (the multi-user scenario gopass's own documentation describes as its intended use case), a crafted entry name that reaches a victim's local store via an ordinary sync causes `gopass rm -r <that entry>` to recursively delete an attacker-chosen directory anywhere the running user has filesystem write access, entirely outside the intended password-store sandbox. `IsDir` returning an incorrect result for a path outside the store root is a secondary, lower-severity issue on its own (it's a read, not a destructive operation), but shares the same missing validation and is fixed alongside `Prune`. ## Suggested Fix Route both `IsDir` and `Prune` through the same `safePath` helper `Get`, `Set`, `Move`, `Delete`, and `Exists` already use, rather than building an unvalidated path directly.

Since then: - the newer `LinkTarget` helper (`internal/backend/storage/fs/link_target.go:17`) **does** apply `safePath` — showing new link-related code follows the guarantee; - `Link` — the method that actually *creates* links — was missed and remains unguarded on master. ### Suggested fix Apply `safePath` to `from` and `to` in `fs.Store.Link` before any filesystem operation (deriving `toDir` from the validated path), and reject traversal components at `leaf.Link` as defense in depth; add a regression test asserting that a `to` containing `../` fails without creating anything outside the store root. ### Proof of concept Dynamic proof at the storage layer (Go test executed against v1.17.3): ```go // internal/backend/storage/fs/link_escape_poc_test.go func TestLinkEscapesStoreRoot(t *testing.T) { store := t.TempDir() outside := t.TempDir() // a different directory = outside the store root s := New(store) os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(store, 'x.gpg'), []byte('SECRETDATA'), 0o600) rel, _ := filepath.Rel(store, outside) to := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join(rel, 'pwned.gpg')) // e.g. '../002/pwned.gpg' if err := s.Link(context.Background(), 'x', to); err != nil { t.Fatalf('Link returned error (no escape happened): %v', err) } // -> PASS: symlink created outside the store root } ``` Output: ``` attacker-supplied to = '../002/pwned.gpg' SYMLINK CREATED OUTSIDE STORE ROOT: /var/folders/…/002/pwned.gpg -> ../001/x ``` (The real chain reaches the same sink: `leaf.Link` passes `s.passfile(ctx, to)` to the storage layer, appending `.gpg`.) A full-CLI reproduction: `gopass init && gopass generate x && gopass link x ../../../../../../tmp/pwned` — `ls -l /tmp/pwned.gpg` shows the symlink outside the store. ### Impact The fs backend's containment guarantee (paths must resolve under the store root) is violated on this method: a destination containing `../` components causes gopass to create arbitrary directories outside the store root (`os.MkdirAll`) and place a symlink there (`os.Symlink`). Threat model, following the project's own GHSA-rw43-4vhf-hcvj: gopass stores are multi-user and git-synced, and a remote collaborator with legitimate write access can reach victims through an ordinary sync. Compared with the fixed `IsDir`/`Prune` vectors (where a synced entry name is enough), this one additionally requires a `gopass link` invocation with an attacker-influenced `to`, so we rate it **Medium** like the sibling advisory (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L ≈ 5.4). Consequences: out-of-store directory creation and symlink planting (a foothold for later read/follow operations, since path resolution is lexical and the OS follows symlinks), and breakage of the store-containment invariant that other tooling may rely on.

GHSA-rw43-4vhf-hcvj.title: Path traversal in Prune and IsDir allows arbitrary recursive directory deletion via a crafted secret name
GHSA-rw43-4vhf-hcvj.description: ## Summary `internal/backend/storage/fs.Store` (the on-disk password-store backend) has a `safePath` helper that validates a name resolves to a path under the store root, and returns an error otherwise. `Get`, `Set`, `Move`, `Delete`, and `Exists` all correctly use it. `IsDir` and `Prune` do not: both build their path with a raw, unguarded `filepath.Join(s.path, filepath.Clean(name))`. `Prune` then calls `os.RemoveAll` on that unguarded path. Since gopass is designed around multi-user, git-synced shared secret stores, an entry name containing `../` sequences, arriving via a normal `git pull`/`gopass sync` from another store member, causes `gopass rm -r <that name>` to recursively delete an attacker-chosen directory anywhere the running user has write access, entirely outside the password store. This is distinct from the store-integrity and local-attacker caveats already documented at github.com/gopasspw/gopass/security: `safePath` already exists and is correctly used by 5 of the 7 `Store` methods, showing filesystem containment (operations staying inside the store root) is an intended guarantee, not something being newly requested; `IsDir` and `Prune` are simply inconsistent with the other five. And the attacker here is a remote git collaborator with legitimate write access to a shared store, reaching the victim through an ordinary sync, not the local-machine attacker the threat model explicitly excludes. ## Details `internal/backend/storage/fs/store.go`: ```go func (s *Store) safePath(name string) (string, error) { resolved := filepath.Join(s.path, filepath.Clean(name)) if !strings.HasPrefix(resolved, s.path+string(filepath.Separator)) { return '', fmt.Errorf('path traversal detected: %q escapes store root', name) } return resolved, nil } func (s *Store) IsDir(ctx context.Context, name string) bool { ... path := filepath.Join(s.path, filepath.Clean(name)) isDir := fsutil.IsDir(path) ... } func (s *Store) Prune(ctx context.Context, prefix string) error { path := filepath.Join(s.path, filepath.Clean(prefix)) ... if err := os.RemoveAll(path); err != nil { return err } return s.removeEmptyParentDirectories(path) } ``` `IsDir` and `Prune` both bypass `safePath` and build their own unvalidated path. `internal/store/leaf/move.go`, the call path from a normal delete: ```go func (s *Store) delete(ctx context.Context, name string, recurse bool) error { path := s.passfile(ctx, name) if recurse { if err := s.deleteRecurse(ctx, name, path); err != nil { return err } } ... } func (s *Store) deleteRecurse(ctx context.Context, name, path string) error { if !s.storage.IsDir(ctx, name) && !s.storage.Exists(ctx, path) { return store.ErrNotFound } name = strings.TrimPrefix(name, string(filepath.Separator)) if err := s.storage.Prune(ctx, name); err != nil { ... } ... } ``` `name` reaches `storage.Prune` unmodified (aside from trimming a leading separator), with no traversal validation at any layer above the storage backend. ## POC (available upon request) ## Impact Confirmed directly against `Store.Prune`: given a store rooted at a directory, calling `Prune` with a name containing `../` segments deletes a directory tree completely outside the store root, with no error returned. Since `gopass rm -r <name>` (recursive delete, one of the tool's core commands) passes the given name to `Prune` unmodified, and since the name of an entry in a shared, git-synced store can be set by any team member with write access to that store (the multi-user scenario gopass's own documentation describes as its intended use case), a crafted entry name that reaches a victim's local store via an ordinary sync causes `gopass rm -r <that entry>` to recursively delete an attacker-chosen directory anywhere the running user has filesystem write access, entirely outside the intended password-store sandbox. `IsDir` returning an incorrect result for a path outside the store root is a secondary, lower-severity issue on its own (it's a read, not a destructive operation), but shares the same missing validation and is fixed alongside `Prune`. ## Suggested Fix Route both `IsDir` and `Prune` through the same `safePath` helper `Get`, `Set`, `Move`, `Delete`, and `Exists` already use, rather than building an unvalidated path directly.
